title: Build a belt scene from the empty floor
summary: Open the Scene editor on an empty floor, place a belt, an emitter, a sensor and a start button with the names the lesson gives, bind their signals in the plant map and write the program that runs on them.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Place the parts of a scene by name and bind each signal of the plant map to a program variable.
Run a program on the scene you built and see the Check grade that scene, not a copy of it.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: Open scene.json in the Scene editor and place four parts with exactly these names: Belt1 (a belt), Emitter1 (an emitter that puts the box on the belt at its near end), EyeFar (a diffuse sensor that must see the box when it reaches the far end of the belt) and StartButton (a push button). In plant-map.json bind StartButton.pressed to BeltToSensor.Start, EyeFar.detect to BeltToSensor.EyeFar, Belt1.run to BeltToSensor.Run and Emitter1.emit to BeltToSensor.Emit. Then, in src/BeltToSensor.ld.json, complete the program: a press of Start puts one box on the belt and runs it, and the belt stops as soon as EyeFar sees the box.
stages.checkpoint: The scene has four parts with those names, the plant map has four signals, and a press of Start puts one box on the belt and runs it until EyeFar sees the box.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, follow the box: the emitter puts it on the near end, the belt carries it to the far end, and the sensor tells the program to stop the belt. A scene that lacks a part the scenario reads cannot do any of that, and the Check says which part it cannot find.
stages.checkpoint: Belt off before the press; on after it, with one box on it; off again as soon as EyeFar sees the box, and it stays off.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save the scene, the plant map and the program, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter scene is an empty floor, so there is nothing to run; place Belt1, Emitter1, EyeFar and StartButton, bind their four signals in the plant map, and write the program that starts the belt and stops it when EyeFar sees the box.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press Run (F5) and open the 3D view.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named build-belt-scene and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the box ride the belt you placed and stop where the beam of the sensor you placed meets it; if EyeFar is missing, read the message of the Check: it names the part and the file where the fix goes.
stages.checkpoint: Run falls when the sensor turns on, not before, and the box is never dropped.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The scenario presses StartButton and reads what EyeFar counted, so a scene without those two names has nothing to grade; the names are part of the contract between the scene, the plant map and the program.
stages.checkpoint: What the assertions check is tested; nothing else is.

hints.text: Show the plant, keep {{ui:plant.panel.projectScene}} selected and press {{ui:plant.panel.editScene}}: the scene of this lesson is the empty floor. Each part you add is named and placed in {{ui:plantEditor.formHeading}}; the reading lists the steps of the editor.

Add a belt, an emitter, a diffuse optical sensor and a push button, and name them Belt1, Emitter1, EyeFar and StartButton. Put Belt1 at X 0, Z 0, Emitter1 at X -1, Z 0, EyeFar at X 0.75, Z -0.5 with rotation 270 and StartButton beside the belt, at X -1, Z -0.75. The settings of the parts may stay at their defaults (the finished scene of the lesson uses a belt length of 2.4, a belt speed of 0.5 and a sensor range of 1). Bind the four signals to the points of the table in the reading, then press {{ui:plantEditor.done}} and {{ui:plant.panel.saveToProject}}. In the program, put a contact on Run in parallel with the Start contact so the belt holds itself on, and keep the EyeFar contact normally closed so it breaks the rung when the box arrives.

faultCases: The starter scene is an empty floor, so there is nothing to run; place Belt1, Emitter1, EyeFar and StartButton, bind their four signals in the plant map, and write the program that starts the belt and stops it when EyeFar sees the box.
